findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Give a concrete AST/symbol-level detection rule for each prohibited category ('credential read', 'backend property reload', 'literal-getattr env equivalent', 'configurable adapter default'), e.g. the receiver/attribute/symbol patterns that trigger each.
evidence: 'literal-getattr env equivalent, backend property reload, credential read, or configurable adapter default'
ABSENCE: no AST-shape or symbol-list definition for 'credential read' or 'backend property reload'
findings.finding: Several prohibited-access categories are named but not operationally defined: 'literal-getattr env equivalent', 'backend property reload', 'credential read', and 'configurable adapter default'. The gate is an AST classifier, so each category needs a concrete detection rule (which AST shape / receiver / symbol names constitute a 'credential read' or 'backend property reload'). As written, the executor must invent these definitions.
scenarios: Executor's notion of 'credential read' differs from the author's, causing either misses or false positives on the real tree
Fixtures pass but real below-seam credential reads go undetected

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the gate resolves env reads through project helper shims (e.g. _rebar_env/_env_int/_str_pref/_llm_int/_int_env/_str_env) — either a KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS-style table mirroring gen_env_registry.py or a structural rule that treats a below-seam helper wrapping os.environ as itself a below-seam access — so a read routed through an existing shim cannot silently bypass the access-kind scan.
evidence: Plan: 'flags any direct or import/local-aliased load_config, os.getenv, os.environ.get, os.environ[...], literal-getattr env equivalent ... that occurs BELOW the approved seams'
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py:87-89 `_rebar_env(name, default) -> os.environ.get(f"REBAR_{name}", default)` — a below-seam env read wrapped in a helper

scripts/gen_env_registry.py:44-46 documents the identical hazard: 'a helper absent from this table is not an error, it is INVISIBLE ... a clean --check proves agreement with the generator, never completeness' and maintains KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS (lines 37-51) precisely to resolve shim indirection
Plan Outcome names the goal as preventing that 'a new ambient load_config/os.getenv read below the central seam can silently reappear'
findings.finding: The gate's prohibited-access mechanism classifies by access KIND at the site (direct/import/local-aliased os.environ/os.getenv/load_config), but the dominant real-tree below-seam read pattern is env reads WRAPPED in project helper shims (e.g. _rebar_env, _env_int, _str_pref, _llm_int, _int_env, _str_env). A below-seam module calling such a shim performs an ambient read the AST access-kind scan cannot see (it sees a local-function call, not an os.environ access), so a new below-seam read added through an existing shim bypasses the gate silently — the exact scenario the plan promises to prevent.
findings.location: Outcome / Plan step 1 (receiver/alias resolution to classify each ambient access)
scenarios: A new below-seam module reads REBAR_FOO via the existing _rebar_env('FOO') shim; the gate reports no finding because it never sees an os.environ access
A refactor introduces a new one-line env helper below the seam and routes reads through it, defeating the access-kind scan
findings.suggested_fix: Add a helper-resolution step to the classifier: enumerate the project env-read helpers (reuse gen_env_registry.py's KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS) and treat a below-seam CALL to any such helper as an ambient access; require new helpers to be registered so an unregistered below-seam env-reading helper is itself a gate failure rather than invisible.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the baseline and mechanism for detecting a 'newly declared' env spelling / credential name (e.g. enumerate from the named registries at run time and require each to map to exactly one owner entry), and name the authoritative config/adapter registry file paths.
evidence: 'the gate fails when a newly declared configurable env spelling or provider credential name has no owner'
'derived from the authoritative config/adapter registries' — registries named but their concrete paths/identities are not given
ABSENCE: no definition of how 'newly' is computed (diff against a checked-in list? enumeration from registry at run time?)
findings.finding: The gate must detect a 'newly declared configurable env spelling or provider-credential name lacking an owner' (AC2), but the plan never specifies the BASELINE against which 'newly' is measured, nor how the gate enumerates the current set of declared spellings/credential names. Without a defined source-of-truth snapshot or derivation, an executor cannot determine what counts as 'new' vs pre-existing.
scenarios: Executor implements a run-time enumeration that treats every unowned name as failing, breaking the 'exits 0 on current tree' AC
Executor cannot decide the mechanism and must stop to ask
findings.suggested_fix: State the exact registry file paths (the 'authoritative config/adapter registries') and specify that the gate enumerates every declared env spelling / credential name from them and fails any that lacks exactly one owner entry — so 'newly declared' == 'present in registry but absent from owner map'.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: The gate re-specifies AST recognition of os.getenv/os.environ.get/os.environ[...]/project env helpers, but scripts/gen_env_registry.py already implements exactly this env-access recognition, so the plan risks a parallel, drift-prone env-access parser.

findings.finding: The plan authors a brand-new independent AST scanner that re-implements env-read detection (os.environ[...]/os.environ.get/os.getenv literals) and env-name enumeration, but scripts/gen_env_registry.py already implements exactly this — including helper-shim resolution (KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS), _deprecations.REGISTRY env-name enumeration (_env_aliases), and derived-name surfacing (MCP_ENV_VARS, alias table). Rebuilding this logic risks duplicating and diverging from the already-solved (and already-tested) env-read detection, and re-encounters the helper-invisibility gap the generator learned to handle.
scenarios: A future env-read spelling handled by gen_env_registry.py's helper table is missed by the new gate because the two scanners diverge
Maintenance cost doubles: every new env helper must be taught to two independent AST scanners
